touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.
Code that is no longer needed is deleted. Git history keeps it if we ever need it back.

Deleting code is about running code, not about the record of what happened. A retired path that something still CALLS is the defect; a retired path named by a record of what passed through (history, state, validations, verdicts, a measured fixture) is not. Requirements that police history are de-emphasized, because the aim is less history noise in front of Claude, not hidden history (Law 5). Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#99 (ticket c8e421aac06e's measured fixture names skills/ruled/intention+why.json and the retirement tooth read it as a caller): "we are trying to remove as much of the history as we can. not hiding it, but reducing the noise you're exposed to. time to de-emphasize requirements like that."
Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

Test tiers. Akien 2026-11-13, from Silicon Spice around 2000: commit, hourly, daily and weekly tests. The complete compiler test ran 40 hours across two executors, so it ran weekly, and the tiers below it meant commit time needed only smoke tests.

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. Akien: "being put in service only requires that it's the best we can do now. only requires 80% trust."

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Akien 2026-11-13: "every test failure, every orphaned file, HAS TO BE FIXED. if we get 3 reds but they're really not related to what we just did, we can ticket them for fixing. reds don't get lost." and "so each run writes any new bugs". Once a red unrelated to a crossing is ticketed, that crossing can go ahead.

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, "because even the basic laws rest finally upon those core principles" (Akien 2026-11-13). Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).

The same boundary runs wherever Akien designed a tool or machine and CC filled in its specific contents: the nest and its questions, the inspectors and their sieves, the gates and their checks, the corrosion set, the skill doors and their field lists. Each such component's charter carries a design_boundary naming what Akien designed, what CC designed, and how a red over CC's part is settled. CC's part is CC's to adjudicate against its own why. Akien may be asked whether a part could be better, with the whys laid out, and whatever CC can't sort goes to him. A new component that has this boundary declares it in its charter when it is born. Akien 2026-11-13: "i think we make a note in the nest and/or sieve tools/machines that the specific contents are at your design. and anywhere else we wind up with an akien/claude boundary. because i'm aware I hadn't thought about that boundary until today."
